title: Lifecycle Toolchain and Role Evolution Handbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This handbook documents the end-to-end lifecycle for Redwood employees from offer acceptance through early career progression. It maps the internal toolchain used during onboarding and day-to-day work, outlines role ladders and promotion expectations, and defines handoffs between People Ops, IT, and manager teams. The goal is predictable, measurable ramp and consistent promotion decisions across teams.

Scope and audience
- Audience: new hires, managers, people-ops partners, engineering leads, recruiting, and IT onboarding specialists.
- Scope: applies to all full-time and permanent-part-time hires across engineering, product, and go-to-market functions. Contractors and vendors follow a parallel but separate access flow (link to vendor onboarding).

Key owners
- People Ops: onboarding flow, offer paperwork, role ladder maintenance, promotion cadence.
- IT / Access Team: account provisioning, SSO/Okta, device imaging.
- Hiring manager & team: role-specific ramp, mentorship, performance reviews.

Role ladders and expectations (summary)
This section provides a concise mapping of our role ladder terminology and the behavioral/impact expectations at each level. Use the competency maps referenced in the related pages for level-specific examples.

Table: IC ladder snapshot
| Level | Title (typical) | Focus | Typical horizon | Core expectations |
|-------|-----------------|-------|-----------------|------------------|
| L1 | Associate / New IC | Deliver under close guidance | 0–1 year | Clear task ownership, reliable delivery, learns the codebase and workflows |
| L2 | IC2 / Contributor | Owns small features end-to-end | 1–2 years | Independent delivery, debugging, cross-team communication |
| L3 | IC3 / Senior IC | Leads medium initiatives | 2–4 years | Technical leadership on projects, mentoring juniors, design reviews |
| L4 | Staff / Principal IC | System-level impact | 4–7 years | Designs cross-service solutions, shapes roadmap, strong technical influence |
| L5 | Senior Principal | Strategic/organization impact | 7+ years | Defines architecture strategy, influences product and org direction |

Promotion and calibration overview
- Promotions are driven by evidence of impact mapped to the competency rubric. Evidence includes shipping history, architecture docs, mentorship examples, customer/peer feedback, and measurable outcomes.
- Calibration occurs quarterly during review cycles; People Ops maintains a promotion checklist and tracks decisions to ensure fairness.

Concrete promotion rubric (scoring matrix)
- Four dimensions assessed for promotions: Technical Ownership, Delivery & Execution, Communication & Influence, Mentorship & Team Health. Each dimension scored on a 1–4 scale; promotion requires an average of >=3.0 and evidence in at least 3 dimensions.

Example: Promotion to IC3 (Senior IC) requires:
1. Two+ projects demonstrating end-to-end ownership and system thinking.
2. Positive peer feedback on design reviews and code quality.
3. Mentorship evidence: mentee growth, code reviews frequency.
4. Clear impact metrics (latency reduction, cost savings, customer satisfaction) when applicable.

Toolchain map: who owns access and when
- Okta (SSO) — IT (automated by People Ops at T+0): primary identity provider for all internal tools.
- Google Workspace — IT: email, calendar, shared drives.
- GitHub (org, team repos) — Engineering IT + team maintainers: repo membership is granted per team template.
- Redwood Console (internal) — Platform team: granted after completion of security training (T+3 days).
- Infra Portal / Cloud Console — Cloud Accounts team: access by role and approval; least-privilege enforced.
- Slack — People Ops/IT: auto-joined channels for team, #announcements, #engineering (guideline to opt-out).
- Confluence — People Ops: read access by default with edit privileges from managers.
- Access Request Service (ARS) — IT: used for elevated privileges requiring approval.

Table: Sample provisioning timeline
| Day | Action | Owner | Required artifacts |
|-----|--------|-------|-------------------|
| Offer signed (T-0) | Trigger provisioning workflow | People Ops | Signed offer doc, ID verification |
| Day 0 | Okta + Google + Slack | IT | Employee record in HRIS |
| Day 0–3 | Laptop imaged & shipped | IT | Device acceptance form |
| Day 1 | Team repo invites & access | Hiring manager | GitHub team assignment |
| Day 3 | Security training + Redwood Console access | People Ops / Platform | Training completion flag |
| Week 1 | First-week 1:1 & onboarding plan | Hiring manager | 30/60/90 plan |

First 90 days: recommended onboarding and ramp plan
- Week 0 (pre-start):
  1. Complete HR paperwork and ID verification.
  2. Set up Okta + Google Workspace; verify Slack and email.
  3. Review the team 30/60/90 template and first-week agenda (link in related pages).
- Week 1: orientation & systems
  1. Day 1: Welcome, benefits overview, security training.
  2. Day 2–5: Pair with buddy, clone repos, run local dev environment, complete at least one small bugfix.
  3. End of week: manager 1:1 to confirm 30/60/90 goals.
- Month 1–2: project ramp and outcomes
  1. Deliver a scoped feature or fix with peer reviews.
  2. Demonstrate knowledge of key services and incident playbooks.
  3. Participate in on-call shadowing if applicable.
- Month 3: graduation & calibration
  1. Present a short "first-quarter demo": what was delivered, technical approach, next steps.
  2. Manager provides formal feedback and updates the performance checkpoint.

First-week operational checklist (numbered)
1. Confirm laptop receipt and sign device acceptance (IT).
2. Sign into Okta and enable 2FA.
3. Join team Slack; post an intro in #team-channel.
4. Clone primary repo and run the test suite locally.
5. Complete mandatory security and privacy training.
6. Meet buddy and schedule recurring 1:1 with manager.
7. Verify access to Redwood Console and Confluence.

Onboarding exceptions and fast-track flows
- Fast-track for experienced hires: a manager may request accelerated provisioning and a condensed ramp. Approval required by People Ops and Security, documented in the onboarding ticket.
- Cross-functional transfers: access to prior-team resources is revoked by default and must be re-requested via ARS with a business justification.

Manager responsibilities during the first 6 months
- Provide a clear 30/60/90 plan and review it weekly in the first month.
- Assign a buddy and at least two short onboarding tasks that touch the codebase, infra, and product.
- Run a 30-day check-in and a formal 90-day performance checkpoint.
- Document outcomes and raise any promotion/concern flags to People Ops with examples.

Device and security baseline (minimum requirements)
- All company laptops must have disk encryption enabled, 2FA for Okta, and approved EDR agent installed.
- Pass mandatory security training; completion required for access to production credentials.

Sample CLI snippets and config examples
- Set up AWS profile for infra sandbox (example):
  $ aws configure --profile redwood-sandbox
  AWS Access Key ID [None]: <provided-key>
  AWS Secret Access Key [None]: <provided-secret>
  Default region name [None]: us-west-2

- GitHub team assignment (example template for managers):
  1. Open GitHub > team > Add member > select new hire.
  2. Confirm repo permissions: write for team repos; contributor for shared libs.

Common onboarding pitfalls and mitigation tips
- Delayed device delivery: keep a small pool of spares and use a temporary cloud-based dev environment for week 1.
- Missing repo permissions: manager should validate access by Day 1 and escalate to Engineering IT if not granted within 24 hours.
- Overloaded first week: prioritize no more than three high-impact orientation items and move others to Week 2.

Continued career development and internal mobility
- People Ops publishes quarterly open roles and internal mobility windows.
- Rotation pilots: staff can apply to short-term rotations (3–6 months) with manager approval; People Ops supports transitions and leveling checks.
- Learning budget: each employee has an annual discretionary learning allowance. Book through the learning portal and tag the expense to the manager-approved project.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Access ownership matrix (quick reference)
  - People Ops: HRIS triggers, benefits enrollment, policy communication.
  - IT: Okta, device imaging, Slack, email, hardware procurement.
  - Platform/Cloud Accounts: production infra access, Redwood Console roles.
  - Hiring manager: GitHub team access, code reviewers, mentorship plan.
- Appendix B: Escalation path for provisioning issues
  1. Submit a ticket to IT via ARS and copy People Ops.
  2. If unresolved in 48 hours, escalate to People Ops manager.
  3. If unresolved in 5 business days, escalate to Head of People Ops with case notes.

Feedback and updates
- This document is reviewed quarterly. To propose edits or add a playbook, open a PR against this page and request review from People Ops. For urgent changes to the onboarding flow (security or compliance), notify People Ops and Security slack channels and attach the proposed change.
